I recommend that the law should not permit assisted dying for individuals with treatment-resistant depression, regardless of their competence or number of previous refusals. Instead, the law should require that such individuals be offered intensive, specialized psychiatric care and therapy, including access to innovative and experimental treatments, before assisted dying can be considered.

In the case of the 29-year-old, I would suggest that the law mandate a comprehensive review of their treatment history and a thorough assessment by a multidisciplinary team of mental health experts to identify any potential alternative treatments or interventions that may have been overlooked. The law should prioritize providing this individual with access to the best possible care and support, rather than assisted dying, to ensure that all avenues for improving their mental health have been exhausted before considering such a drastic measure.
